product_question: Does TRIBUNAL's H.R. 1702 federal district-court capacity envelope establish an admissible JUS savings candidate or change Taxlane's rate result?

official_fiscal_path.accounting_rule: Direct judge compensation and appropriated court operations are added once. No delay, detention, litigant, prosecution, defense, corrections, or social savings are scored.

taxlane_assessment.reason: H.R. 1702 is a distinct proposed capacity investment rather than the existing selected-DOJ-grant reduction. It is not enacted, CBO does not score caseflow or rights outcomes, and district allocation, version, appropriation, appointment, staffing, delivery, incidence, rights-floor, and overlap evidence remain incomplete.

level_2_requirements: exact amended reported-bill text reconciled to CBO's 65 permanent judgeship count
enactment, appropriation, appointments, confirmations, staffed seats, and district milestones
district and case-type filing-to-disposition, aged-pending, vacancy, senior-judge, and magistrate baselines
counsel, liberty, victim notice, evidence integrity, disparity, and durable-resolution policy and stress results
district allocation, litigant incidence, and geographic distribution review
prosecution, defense, detention, corrections, facilities, security, and technology overlap reconciliation
reviewed service-floor passage and candidate-specific Taxlane admission rerun
public_warning: TRIBUNAL now supplies a real, replayable H.R. 1702 federal district-court capacity envelope. It adds a new held JUS identity and reconciles $111 million direct and $283 million appropriated outlays to $394 million through FY2035. More judgeships and higher court spending do not by themselves prove faster, safer, fairer, or cheaper justice. No savings are admitted and no rate changes.
